PGE2 inhibits lipopolysacchride-induced IL-12 production in monocytes and that this effect is not mediated by IL-10.
prostaglandin-E2 (PGE(2)) inhibits the production of interleukin-12 (IL-12), which is essential for induction of Th1 immune responses.
prostaglandin-E2 inhibits IL-12 synthesis in monocytes, whereas IL-10 production is enhanced, resulting in a Th2 response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of prostaglandins in immune regulation.
the role of PGE2 in the regulation of IL-12 production.
the regulation of IL-12 and other Th1 cytokines by PGE2 and IL-10, and their possible role in the induction of Th2 responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PGE2, by its capacity to inhibit IL-12 synthesis, can contribute to a Th2 response.
PGE2 is an important inhibitor of IL-12 production and thus of Th1 development.
the production of PGE2 by antigen presenting cells may play an important role in determining the outcome of the immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of PGE2 by antigen presenting cells may play an important role in the development and maintenance of a Th2 response.
the Th2 response is a result of the overproduction of PGE2, which in turn inhibits IL-12 production.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PGE2 is an inhibitor of human IL-12 production and this effect is mediated by the induction of cAMP.
prostaglandin-E2 (PGE-2) is a potent inhibitor for the production of human interleukins 12, 6, and 10.
